..
KEY MESSAGE 1...

A cold front remains across eastern New England and NJ this
afternoon. A low pressure system is moving across the PA-MD
border. Low and mid level warm advection is increasing across
northeast PA into central-eastern NY with developing showers
with support from the right entrance region of an upper level 
jet streak over upstate NY. The best low to mid level FGEN in 
the H850-700 layer is south and east of the Capital Region this 
afternoon into early tonight. PWATs have risen into the 1.3-1.7"
range from the Greater Capital Region south to the I-84 
corridor in southern Ulster, Dutchess and Litchfield Counties. 
PoPs were increased into the slight to chance range as far 
north as the Mohawk River Valley, southern reaches of the Lake 
George Saratoga Region and southern VT. The highest PoPs in the 
55-80% range continue to be across the eastern Catskills, mid 
Hudson Valley, southern Taconics, southern Berkshires and 
Litchfield Counties, where the better forcing overlaps with the 
moisture convergence. 

WPC continues a Marginal Risk (Level 1 of 4)in th Day 1 ERO for
the locations just north of I-84 in southern Ulster, Dutchess 
and Litchfield Counties for isolated instance of flash flooding.
The gridded 1-hr FFG remains high in these areas in the 
1.8-2.5" range, and the 3-hr values are generally 2.5-3". The 
latest HREFs shows rates of 0.1-0.25"/hr into tonight with 
briefly higher amounts of 0.25-0.50"/hr. The high FFG values and
the rainfall rates not too high is why we held issuing a Flood 
Watch. Some poor drainage flooding of low-lying and urban areas 
may occur. We kept thunder out of the forecast with very little 
instability of less than 300 J/kg south and east of Albany in 
the HREF. We also used the WPC QPF with basin average amounts of
0.50-1.00" over the mid Hudson Valley, eastern Catskills, 
southern Taconics and Litchfield, CT. Localized amounts of 1-2" 
may occur if any higher rainfall amounts occur or training. 
Expect higher amounts further north of a tenth to a quarter inch
to the Capital Region and southern VT and a trace to a few 
hundredths of an inch. The showers should end quickly from 
northwest to southeast shortly before or just after midnight. 
The skies will become mostly clear to partly cloudy, especially
northwest of the mid Hudson Valley/NW CT with some patchy to 
areas of fog developing in the valleys. Lows fall back into the 
50s with some 40 over the southwest Adirondacks. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...

High pressure builds in from southern Quebec with a mainly a 
dry day across eastern NY and western New England with dewpoints
in the 50s to lower 60s, so humidity levels will be comfortable.
Max temps will be seasonal in the 70s to lower 80s with a few 
upper 60s over the higher terrain. A mid and upper level trough
begins to dig in Fri night from south of James Bay across the 
Great Lakes Region/Ohio Valley. A southern stream short-wave 
moves northeast of the TN Valley into the mid-Atlantic Region 
Sat morning along the eastern periphery of the deepening 
trough. Clouds increase with the greatest probabilities for 
showers and a few thunderstorms south and east of the Capital 
Region during the afternoon into the evening. We lowered PoPs to
the 15-20% range from Albany north and west Saturday until the 
next short-wave approaches from the south and west for Sat 
night into Sunday. The ensembles and short-range guidance shows 
some spread with the timing of these features. WPC continues a 
Marginal Risk (Level 1 of 4) in the Day 3 ERO for southeast 
Dutchess, Litchfield Counties. If showers or thunderstorms 
repeatedly move over the same area with excessive rainfall rates
and with wetter antecedent conditions, then an isolated flash 
flood can not be ruled out. Temps will tend to run slightly 
cooler than normal on Sat with mid 60 to lower 70s over the 
higher terrain and mid and upper 70s in the valleys. 

The broad, mid and upper level trough shifts from a neutral
tilt to negative tilt over NY and New England with the closed
H500 low south of James Bay. A low pressure system and a sfc
trough or occluded front will bring periods of showers and a few
thunderstorms on Sunday. PoPs continues continue in the 70 to
95% range. The NBM 24-hr Probs for >0.50" of rainfall by 
00Z/Mon are in the 30-50% range across eastern NY and western 
New England with highest Probs over the Mohawk Valley and 
southwest Dacks. The rainfall should be mainly beneficial, as 
the previous discussion noted. Temps continue to run near or 
slightly below normal to close the weekend and open next week. 
The upper level low begins to move away Mon into Tue with 
lingering cyclonic flow and upslope/instability showers over the
higher terrain with seasonal temps for late AUG.
